name: Corn Farming (Animal Manure Land Management with Energy Allocation)
notes:
In this scenario, animal manure is applied to the soil at any point during the corn growing season in a corn-soy rotation. The land management change scenario considers energy allocation of all corn farming, stover collection, and cover crop management inputs, Also defined by this scenario is a 30% stover removal rate, US average tillage, and a yield increase every year over the 30 year corn-soy rotation.

Note:This process has been modified after we discovered that Sodium hydroxide, Sodium hydroxide and Hydrochloric acid were mistakenly input as energy shares instead of mass amounts.  Now that these chemicals are treated as non-energy products, their inputs are changed to mass amounts and the energy shares have to be re-balanced among NG, electricity and MeOH.  Below is the copy of the emai messagel from Jeongwoo Han for reference:

For the transesterification process (BD production), use the following assumptions.
Total Energy Inputs (Btu/lb. of BD): 1,213
Shares of Process Fuels: NG 30.7%; Electricity 4.6%; MeOH 64.7%
Other chemical (lb/lb of BD): Sodium hydroxide 0.000972; Sodium methoxide 0.023105; Hydrochloric acid 0.043376; Phosphoric acid 0.000999; Citric acid 0.000729
 
We have sodium hydroxide, hydrochloric acid and phosphoric acid, but no sodium methoxide and citric acid.
For sodium methoxide, use methanol as a surrogate. For citric acid, don? put an upstream.

Both Methanol input contains CO2 input emission ratio of 137.5% (C ratio of methanol/C ratio of CO2=0.375/12*44)
The Methanol in upper input box is actually sodium methoxide; methanol in group input is methanol.
